answerKey.primaryProblem: Perimenopausal vasomotor/sleep symptoms with overdue preventive cancer screening (cervical and colorectal) and unknown hepatitis B status in a patient born in an endemic region
differential: Perimenopause (most likely given age, irregular cycles, hot flushes, and supportive but non-diagnostic FSH/estradiol pattern)
Primary ovarian insufficiency (less likely at 46 with gradual pattern)
Thyroid dysfunction (ruled out by normal TSH)
Occupational irritant contact dermatitis of hands (separate, lower-acuity issue)
Anemia from heavy perimenopausal bleeding (screened with CBC, currently normal)
keyFindings: 8 months of irregular periods, hot flushes, and poor sleep consistent with perimenopause
FSH elevated and estradiol low on a single, non-cycle-timed draw - supportive of but not diagnostic for perimenopausal transition given expected hormonal fluctuation and undocumented cycle day
Pap smear overdue by several years (last at ~39, now 46) with no documented HPV co-testing
Never screened for colorectal cancer; father died of colon cancer at age 58 (first-degree relative, early-onset) raising her risk category
Hepatitis B serostatus never checked despite birth in Vietnam, a region of intermediate/high endemicity
Mild hand dermatitis temporally linked to acrylic/solvent exposure at work, improves with time off
plan: Discuss perimenopause as the likely clinical diagnosis based on symptom pattern; explain that the FSH/estradiol result is supportive but, drawn without a documented cycle day, cannot be treated as definitive given normal perimenopausal hormone fluctuation; further hormonal workup is not urgently needed unless symptoms worsen or red flags develop
Offer options for symptom management (lifestyle measures, consider low-dose hormonal or non-hormonal therapy per shared decision-making) and arrange follow-up to discuss further
Schedule in-person Pap smear with HPV co-testing given 7-year interval and move her onto an appropriate screening schedule going forward

Given father's colon cancer at 58 (first-degree relative under 60), recommend she needs colonoscopy rather than average-risk stool testing alone; refer to gastroenterology for a diagnostic/screening colonoscopy (action a17) and use FIT (action a12) only as an interim/bridge if colonoscopy will be delayed
Order hepatitis B serologic panel given birth in an endemic country; if susceptible, offer hepatitis B vaccination series; if chronic infection found, refer to hepatology/GI for monitoring
Advise on hand dermatitis: barrier creams, gloves during acrylic work, moisturizing; consider topical steroid for flares; refer to dermatology if it worsens or does not respond
Confirm mammography is up to date and will be due per age-based interval; document family history formally in the chart
Address occupational exposure to solvents/acrylic dust - encourage ventilation and glove use at the salon; monitor skin
redFlags: Postmenopausal or intermenstrual bleeding (would warrant endometrial evaluation, not covered by routine perimenopause workup)
Rectal bleeding, unexplained weight loss, or iron-deficiency anemia (would accelerate colorectal workup)
Signs of acute hepatitis or elevated liver enzymes (would need urgent hepatology referral)
Severe or spreading dermatitis with signs of infection (would need prompt dermatology/urgent care)
educationPoints: Family history of early-onset colorectal cancer in a first-degree relative changes screening strategy from average-risk stool-based testing to colonoscopy starting earlier/more intensively, with colonoscopy as the primary recommendation and FIT only as a bridge if colonoscopy is delayed
Patients born in hepatitis B-endemic countries should be screened regardless of risk perception, since perinatal transmission is often asymptomatic for decades

Perimenopause is primarily a clinical diagnosis based on age and symptom pattern; a single random (non-cycle-timed) FSH/estradiol draw is unreliable in a patient with irregular cycles like hers (22-50 day range) because levels fluctuate widely across the cycle and from cycle to cycle, so the result should be used as supportive context rather than a stand-alone diagnostic test

Culturally, patients who tend to agree readily ('yes doctor') may underreport symptoms or defer screening due to time/income pressure; explicit, non-judgmental elicitation and flexible scheduling matter
Occupational irritant dermatitis in nail technicians is common and usually improves with barrier precautions rather than requiring systemic treatment

facts.chart: Patient presents for preventive health visit at adult daughter's urging; reports feeling well overall but notes irregular periods, hot flushes, and poor sleep for 8 months
facts.says: I feel fine, really. My daughter made me come in - she worries too much. I guess my periods have been strange lately and I don't sleep so good.

facts.chart: Menstrual cycles irregular over past 8 months, varying from 22 to 50 days, no change in flow heaviness reported
facts.says: Sometimes it comes early, sometimes it's late by weeks. I never know when to expect it anymore.

facts.chart: Patient tracks cycles using phone calendar app; agrees to share pattern
facts.says: I actually write it down on my phone because it was getting confusing. I can show you.

facts.chart: Hot flushes occur several times daily, lasting a few minutes, with flushing and sweating, worse at night
facts.says: I get these waves of heat, mostly at night. I wake up sweating and have to change my shirt sometimes.

facts.chart: Difficulty staying asleep for 8 months, wakes 2-3 times nightly, feels tired during workday
facts.says: I wake up a lot in the night. By the time I open the salon I am already tired.

facts.chart: No intermenstrual bleeding or postcoital bleeding reported
facts.says: No, nothing like that between times. Just the regular period, just whenever it decides to show up.

facts.chart: No increase in menstrual flow or clotting reported
facts.says: The flow itself is about the same as always, not heavier.

facts.chart: No unintentional weight loss or gain reported
facts.says: My weight has been about the same, I think.

facts.chart: No change in bowel habits, no blood in stool, no abdominal pain reported
facts.says: My stomach is fine, nothing unusual there.

facts.chart: Reports mild irritability but denies significant low mood or anxiety; attributes irritability to poor sleep
facts.says: I get a little short-tempered with my staff sometimes, but I think that's just because I'm so tired.

facts.chart: No prior major medical diagnoses; no history of diabetes, hypertension, or thyroid disease
facts.says: I've never really been sick with anything big. No diabetes, no blood pressure problems that I know of.

facts.chart: No prior surgeries
facts.says: No surgeries, never had one.

facts.chart: Father died of colon cancer at age 58; patient initially does not mention this unprompted
facts.says: My father... he passed away from colon cancer when he was 58. It was a long time ago now.

facts.chart: Mother has hypertension, otherwise no known family history of breast, ovarian, or other cancers
facts.says: My mother has high blood pressure. Nobody else that I know of had cancer.

facts.chart: Works 6 days/week as nail salon owner, long hours, limited time for medical appointments
facts.says: I own the salon, so if I'm not there, nobody is. I work six days a week, it's hard to take time off.

facts.chart: Daily occupational exposure to acrylic dust, nail polish/solvent fumes; ventilation at salon described as 'okay'
facts.says: We use the acrylic powder and the polish removers all day. The ventilation, it's okay, we have a fan.

facts.chart: Intermittent dry, itchy, cracked skin on hands for about a year, worse after work, improves on days off
facts.says: My hands get dry and itchy, sometimes cracked a little. It's better when I take a day away from the chemicals.

facts.chart: Born in Vietnam, immigrated to the US in her 20s
facts.says: I was born in Vietnam. I came here when I was in my twenties.

facts.chart: Patient unsure if she has ever been tested for hepatitis B; no vaccination record known
facts.says: Hepatitis B? I don't think anyone ever checked that. Maybe when I was a kid in Vietnam, I'm not sure.

facts.chart: Last Pap smear approximately 7 years ago at a community clinic; does not recall if HPV testing was done
facts.says: My last pap was a long time ago, maybe seven years? I just kept putting it off because of work.

facts.chart: Never had a colonoscopy, FIT, or any stool-based colorectal screening test
facts.says: No, I've never done that colon test. Nobody told me I needed one.

facts.chart: Last mammogram approximately 3 years ago, reported normal
facts.says: I had the mammogram maybe three years ago. They said it was fine.

facts.chart: Sexually active with husband, monogamous, no new partners
facts.says: I'm married, just my husband. We've been together a long time.

facts.chart: Never smoker
facts.says: No, I've never smoked.

facts.chart: Drinks alcohol rarely, less than once a month, no binge pattern
facts.says: I almost never drink, maybe a sip at a holiday dinner.

facts.chart: Diet mostly home-cooked Vietnamese food, moderate rice intake, patient reports trying to 'eat healthy'
facts.says: I cook at home mostly, rice and vegetables, I try to eat healthy.

facts.chart: Remains physically active standing/walking most of workday at salon; no exercise limitation reported
facts.says: I'm on my feet all day at the salon, so I move a lot, but I don't really 'exercise' exercise.

facts.chart: Expresses concern about missing work income and finding coverage for salon if additional appointments are needed
facts.says: If I have to go to more appointments, who will run the salon? I lose money every day I'm not there.

facts.chart: Tends to verbally agree with medical recommendations readily; daughter later reports some recommendations in the past were not followed through
facts.says: Yes, yes, okay doctor, whatever you think is best.

facts.chart: Patient's main hope for visit is to feel less tired and sleep better; screening tests are not her initial priority
facts.says: I just want to sleep better and have more energy. That's really what I want to fix.

facts.chart: No joint pain, no urinary urgency/frequency, no vaginal dryness volunteered
facts.says: No pain in my joints, no bathroom problems or anything like that.

facts.chart: Takes a daily multivitamin; occasional ibuprofen for headaches, no hormonal medications or supplements for menopause
facts.says: Just a multivitamin every day, and sometimes ibuprofen if my head hurts.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient believes her last Pap smear, about 7 years ago, was simply 'normal' and does not mention whether HPV testing was included
mismatches.recordEvidence: Outside records summary confirms a Pap 7 years ago documented as normal cytology but explicitly notes no HPV co-testing was performed, and no further screening since - meaning she is now significantly overdue regardless of that past normal result
mismatches.teachingPoint: A single past 'normal' result does not mean a patient is up to date; interval and co-testing status must be checked, not assumed from patient recollection alone

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient readily agrees to all recommendations in the moment ('yes, yes, okay doctor')
mismatches.recordEvidence: Family history field was found blank in the chart before today despite the patient having had prior visits, suggesting previous verbal agreement to provide information or follow up did not translate into documented action or follow-through
mismatches.teachingPoint: Verbal agreement, especially from patients who tend to acquiesce to avoid conflict, should be confirmed with teach-back and concrete follow-up plans rather than assumed to equal understanding or completed action

objectives.text: Elicit a focused history of perimenopausal symptoms (irregular cycles, vasomotor symptoms, sleep disruption) and correctly interpret supportive hormone labs without over-relying on them

Proactively screen for and update colorectal cancer risk by eliciting family history that the patient does not volunteer spontaneously, and apply an increased-risk screening strategy (colonoscopy referral, with FIT only as an interim bridge)
Identify overdue cervical cancer screening and recognize that a past 'normal' result without co-testing does not satisfy current screening intervals
Recognize hepatitis B screening indication based on country of birth and order appropriate serologic testing
Assess occupational hand dermatitis related to salon chemical exposure and provide scope-appropriate counseling and triage (self-care vs dermatology referral)
Address psychosocial and systemic barriers to preventive care (time off work, income loss, tendency to acquiesce) and negotiate a realistic, patient-centered follow-up plan

patient.name: Mai Tran
patient.appearance: A trim woman in her mid-40s with shoulder-length dark hair pulled back, wearing a casual salon smock top, seated in a small back office with shelves of nail polish bottles visible behind her. Lighting is a bit dim and overhead; she glances occasionally toward the door as if listening for the salon floor, and her affect is pleasant but slightly hurried and tired-looking.

persona.personality: Warm, hardworking, deferential to authority figures, tends to minimize her own complaints and prioritize work and family obligations over her own health
persona.communicationStyle: Polite and agreeable, answers questions directly but briefly, may initially downplay symptoms or defer sensitive topics unless asked gently and directly, uses simple everyday language
persona.emotionalState: Mildly anxious about taking time off work, slightly embarrassed about bringing up menopause-related symptoms, otherwise calm and cooperative
persona.background: Immigrated from Vietnam in her twenties, built a nail salon business from scratch with her husband, works six days a week and considers the shop her main responsibility; has two adult children, one of whom (her daughter) manages a lot of the family's health-related scheduling and insisted on this visit; proud of being self-sufficient and rarely seeks medical care for herself
speechExamples: I feel fine, really, my daughter just worries too much.
If I'm not at the shop, nobody is, so I try not to miss days.
Yes, yes, okay doctor, whatever you think is best.
My father, he passed from colon cancer, but that was a long time ago.
I just want to sleep better, that's really what I want.
concerns: Losing income or clients if she needs to take time off for appointments
Whether what she's feeling is 'just normal' aging or something she should worry about
Not wanting to seem like she is complaining or wasting the doctor's time
Finding someone to cover the salon for any follow-up visits or procedures

profile.title: Perimenopause and Overdue Preventive Screening in a Busy Nail Salon Owner
profile.summary: Mai Tran, a 46-year-old Vietnamese-American nail salon owner, presents for a preventive visit prompted by her daughter, with 8 months of irregular periods, hot flushes, and poor sleep consistent with perimenopause. The case teaches learners to proactively uncover overdue cervical and colorectal cancer screening (including a reluctantly-disclosed early-onset paternal colon cancer history) and unaddressed hepatitis B risk from birth-country endemicity, while respectfully navigating time/income barriers and a patient's tendency to acquiesce verbally without necessarily following through.
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home in a back office of her nail salon in Houston, Texas
